correctness.rationale: The exact mixed-measure Gram matrix is diag(1,(1+w)/2,(1-w)/2), yielding K=1+(2/(1+w))cos(theta)cos(phi)+(2/(1-w))sin(theta)sin(phi). The absolute row norm equals q I(R(t))+w max(1,at), with I(R)=(2/pi)[sqrt(R^2-1)+arcsin(1/R)]. Its strict t-decrease for t>0 follows from the endpoint bound min_{s in [a^2,b^2]}sqrt(s-1)/s > pi q/8 and t>=(1+w)/2; this is proved using 2sqrt(3)>pi, not inferred from experiments. Thus only perpendicular evaluation points attain the operator norm. Sign kernels attain equality, and positivity off two non-atomic zeros classifies all norming inputs. Elementary differentiation establishes the sharp increasing convex profile and one-sided limits. value.rationale: The mixed continuous/discrete least-squares projection is a naturally parameterized sampling model. Its sharp L∞ amplification, exact maximizing evaluation geometry and sign witnesses, monotone convex dependence on the mass weight, and nontrivial singular limit are meaningful conditioning information not furnished by the mass-update kernel alone. The result is the complete solution for all 0<w<1, rather than an arbitrary isolated parameter computation.
